html:
SMTO-SKL-0006 — SMTO can't find the saved API key this Skill points to

GUID: 40255408-adc6-4548-85e4-d9e46e767e12
Slug: skill-parameter-reference-unavailable
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: skl

What happened

  • This Skill's settings point to a Parameter Store entry, or a field inside it, that isn't there now, for example because it was renamed or deleted. SMTO didn't use the key, so the provider that needs it wasn't contacted.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Settings, open Details and tools, then Skills. Select Configure on the Skill, such as Web, and note its Parameter Store key and Credential field pointer. These two boxes show exactly which entry and field SMTO tried to read.
  2. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu and look for that entry. Check it still exists under that exact name and contains the field the pointer names. A renamed or deleted entry, or a renamed field inside it, makes the reference lead nowhere.
  3. Either restore the entry under the old name, or change the two boxes in the Skill's settings to the entry and field that hold the key now, then select Save. SMTO follows only the exact name and field saved in the Skill's settings.
  4. If the Skill offers Test connection, select it for that provider. The test reads the key and contacts the provider without starting a Task.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Connected, or your next request uses the provider without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the API key into the Skill settings or a conversation to get around this; it must stay in Parameter Store.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Credential resolution found no Parameter Store record under the referenced exact key, or the reference's JSON Pointer does not resolve to a field in that record's value.

What this means

  • Credential resolution cannot find the exact Parameter Store entry or resolve the referenced JSON pointer. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Credential resolution cannot find the exact Parameter Store entry or resolve the referenced JSON pointer.

How to diagnose it

  • Check normalized entry identity and exact pointer against the authorized stored profile.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the referenced parameter_key exists in Parameter Store under the same normalized key and that its pointer resolves within the record's value_json (resolve_credential_reference at use time, SkillConfigurationStore._check_references at save time). Restore the entry, or update the Skill configuration to the current key and field without revealing the value, then run the Skill's Test connection.
  • Check the exact entry and field reference in Parameter Store. Restore the intended entry or select a current field without exposing its value.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The reference resolves privately to the intended credential field.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
